title: State-change retention is unsound: the semantic state omits the fold's accumulators
found_in: experiments/s010/retain.ts (retainByStateChange), the S010 candidate mechanism for fold-derived retention
requirement_violated: A retained history R is sufficient for H iff semanticState(derive(H)) == semanticState(derive(R)), stateHash equal, worldDiff empty. M-H violates this.
description: M-H keeps an intervention iff applying it changes the semantic world, using derive as the oracle. This assumes the semantic state captures everything a later intervention depends on. It does not: the fold's accumulators (negated, forcedBy, retracted, overriddenCells) are NOT part of effectiveSemanticState. An intervention can be a semantic no-op while still setting an accumulator entry that changes what a later intervention means.

minimal_counterexample.cause: forceEvent on an already-ESTABLISHED root event does not change the semantic state, so M-H drops it. But buildModel sets forcedBy[ev/maren-return]; a later negateEvent then yields a force-vs-negate contradiction (CONTRADICTORY) rather than EXCLUDED.

scope: Not limited to the seed canon or to events. Every accumulator (negated/forcedBy/retracted/overriddenCells) has the same property. M-H failed 238/517 (verrin) and 220/517 (ordos) differential cases across every operation. The failure is a property of the retention CRITERION, not of any single operation.
relationship_to_ncr_006: Same structural failure class as NCR-006 (a no-op operation whose accumulator entry becomes observable later), but on the EVENT-STATUS dimension instead of fact identity, and with a shorter witness (2 interventions vs 3). NCR-006 breaks accumulator-only retention (M-B); NCR-007 breaks state-change retention (M-H). Together they show neither observable is sufficient.
proposed_correction: Have the authoritative fold emit, per intervention, whether it changed the FOLD STATE (accumulators + effective facts), not merely the semantic state. A retention driven by that flag is sound by construction and introduces no second semantic authority, because the flag is produced by the fold itself. This requires a src/ change and is left for a separate productionization task.
recommendation: Do not adopt any state-change-based retention. Do not adopt accumulator-only retention (incomplete, NCR-006). The target architecture (full history -> fold -> retained history) is not realizable from the current fold's public outputs.
